'''Paul Joseph Sally Jr.''' (January 29, 1933 – December 30, 2013) was a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Chicago]],<ref>
{{cite web|url=http://www.math.uchicago.edu/people/ |title=Department of Mathematics: People|access-date=2008-09-16|publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref> where he was the director of undergraduate studies for 30 years.<ref name="Chicago Maroon death notice"/><ref>
{{cite web|url=http://www.math.uchicago.edu/about|title=Department of Mathematics: About|access-date=2008-09-16 |publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref> His research areas were [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]] and [[representation theory]].<ref name="UC Mag 2008">{{cite journal|last=Golus|first=Carrie|date=May–June 2008|title=Sally marks the spot|journal=University of Chicago Magazine|volume=100|issue=4|url=http://magazine.uchicago.edu/0856/features/sally.shtml|access-date=2008-09-16}}</ref>

==Life and education==
Sally was born in the [[Roslindale, Boston, Massachusetts|Roslindale]] neighborhood of [[Boston|Boston, Massachusetts]] on January 29, 1933.<ref name="AMS Candidate Bios">{{cite journal |date=September 2002|title=Biographies of Candidates|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=49|issue=8|pages=970–81|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200208/bios02.pdf|access-date=2008-09-16}}</ref><ref name="Globe 2007"/> He was a star basketball player at [[Boston College High School]].<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/><ref name="Globe 2007"/> He received his [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] and [[Master of Science|MS]] degrees from [[Boston College]] in 1954 and 1956.<ref name="Amoco award"/>

After a short career in Boston area high schools and at Boston College,<ref name="BC Sally Award">{{cite web|publisher=Boston College|title=Sally Award|access-date=2008-09-17|url=http://www.bc.edu/schools/cas/math/ugprog/awards.html}}</ref> he entered the first class of mathematics graduate students at [[Brandeis University|Brandeis]] in 1957,<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/> and earned his PhD in 1965.<ref name="AMS Candidate Bios"/> During his graduate career he married [[Judith D. Sally]] and had three children in three years. David, the oldest, is a Visiting Associate Professor of Business Administration at [[Tuck School of Business]] at [[Dartmouth College]],<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/><ref name="David Sally Dartmoth">{{cite web|url=http://www.tuck.dartmouth.edu/faculty/faculty-directory/david-f-sally|title= Tuck School of Business Faculty Directory|publisher=Dartmouth College|access-date=2011-05-08}}</ref> Stephen is a partner at [[White & Case]]<ref name="Stephen Sally White & Case">{{cite web|url=http://www.ropesgray.com/stephenmoeller-sally|title=White & Case Professional Directory|publisher=White & Case|access-date=2024-10-23|archive-date=July 20, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720174851/http://www.ropesgray.com/stephenmoeller-sally/|url-status=dead}}</ref> (previously [[Ropes & Gray]]),<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/><ref name="Stephen Sally Ropes & Gray">{{cite web|url=https://www.whitecase.com/people/stephen-moeller-sally|title=Ropes & Gray Professional Directory|publisher=Ropes & Gray|access-date=2011-05-08}}</ref> and Paul, the youngest, is Superintendent at [[New Trier High School]].<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/><ref name="Paul Sally New Trier">{{cite web|url=http://www.newtrier.k12.il.us/person.aspx?id=3332|title=New Trier High School Staff Directory|publisher=New Trier High School|access-date=2011-05-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110125230615/http://www.newtrier.k12.il.us/person.aspx?id=3332|archive-date=2011-01-25}}</ref>

Sally was diagnosed with [[Diabetes mellitus type 1|type 1 diabetes]] in 1948.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Shaw|first=Susan|date=March 2004|title=Keeping Your Toes & Feet Healthy|journal=Diabetes Health|url=http://www.diabeteshealth.com/read/2004/03/01/3173.html|access-date=2008-09-16|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080510104528/http://www.diabeteshealth.com/read/2004/03/01/3173.html|archive-date=2008-05-10}}</ref> The condition resulted in his use of an [[eye patch]] and two [[prosthetic]] legs,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/paul-j-sally-jr-influential-mathematician-and-educator-1933-2013|title=Paul J. Sally, Jr., influential mathematician and educator, 1933 – 2013|date=2 January 2014}}</ref> which caused him to be widely referred to as "Professor Pirate," and "The Math Pirate" around the [[University of Chicago]] campus.<ref name="Globe 2007">{{cite web|publisher=The Boston Globe|title=The powerhouse 'pirate' of the math classroom|access-date=2008-04-15|author=Billy Baker|date=2007-10-01|url=http://www.boston.com/yourlife/health/articles/2007/10/01/the_powerhouse_pirate_of_the_math_classroom/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071006024436/http://www.boston.com/yourlife/health/articles/2007/10/01/the_powerhouse_pirate_of_the_math_classroom/|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 6, 2007}}</ref> He was known to detest cell phones in class and destroyed several over the years by inviting students to stomp on them or by throwing them out of a window.<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/>

==Career==
Sally joined the [[University of Chicago]] faculty in 1965 and taught there until his death.<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/> He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1967–68, 1971–72, 1981–82, and 1983–84.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ias.edu/people/past-alpha?letter=S |title=Past Members Alphabetical: S &#124; IAS School of Mathematics |website=Math.ias.edu |date=29 August 2008 |access-date=2016-10-21}}</ref>

While at the IAS he collaborated with [[Joseph Shalika]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sally Jr | first1 = P. J. | last2 = Shalika | first2 = J.A. | year = 1968 | title = Characters of the discrete series of representations of SL(2) over a local field | journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | volume = 61 | issue = 4| pages = 1231–1237 | pmid = 16591722 | pmc=225245 | doi=10.1073/pnas.61.4.1231| bibcode = 1968PNAS...61.1231S | doi-access = free }}</ref> In 1983, he became the first director of the [[University of Chicago School Mathematics Project]], which is responsible for the [[Everyday Mathematics]] program (also called "Chicago math").<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/>

He founded Seminars for Elementary Specialists and Mathematics Educators (SESAME) in 1992.<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/> He co-founded the Young Scholars Program with Dr. Diane Herrmann in 1988, providing mathematical enrichment for gifted Chicago-area students in grades 7–12.<ref name="UC Mag 2008"/><ref name="AMS newsletter 2004">{{cite journal|date=Winter 2004|title=Paul Sally Gives the Arnold Ross Lecture|journal=AMS Member Newsletter|page=4|url=https://www.ams.org/membership/membnewsltr-winter2004.pdf|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2008-09-16}}</ref>

==Death==
[[File:Graves of Paul Joseph Sally Jr. (1933–2013) and Judith Donovan Sally (1937–2024) at Maryhill Catholic Cemetery, Niles, IL.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Graves of Paul and Judith Sally at Maryhill Catholic Cemetery]]

Sally died December 30, 2013, aged 80, from [[congestive heart failure]], at the University of Chicago Hospital, and was buried at Maryhill Catholic Cemetery in Niles, Illinois.<ref name="Chicago Maroon death notice">{{cite news |last=Crane|first=Joy|date=2013-12-30|title=Paul Sally, influential math professor, dies at 80|url=http://chicagomaroon.com/2013/12/30/paul-sally-influential-math-professor-dies-at-80/ |newspaper=[[Chicago Maroon]]|access-date=2013-12-30}}</ref><ref name="obit">[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/chicagotribune/obituary.aspx?n=paul-sally&pid=168855049&fhid=3566 Paul Sally Jr. Obituary], ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', retrieved 2014-01-01.</ref><ref name="Chicago Tribune Obituary">{{cite news|title=Chicago Tribune Obituary|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/ct-obit-paul-sally-met-20140116,0,4755459.story|access-date=16 January 2014|newspaper=Chicago Tribune}}</ref>

* Amoco Foundation Award for Long-Term Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching, 1995<ref name="Amoco award">
{{cite news |first=Diana |last=Steele |title=Amoco Teaching Award: Paul Sally |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/950525/sally.shtml |work=University of Chicago Chronicle |date=1995-05-25 |access-date=2008-09-16 }}</ref><ref name="Chronicle Math appreciation">
{{cite news |first=Steve |last=Koppes  |title=Sally says students need more than math 'appreciation' |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/030123/math.shtml |work=University of Chicago Chronicle |date=2003-01-23 |access-date=2008-09-16 }}</ref>
* [[American Mathematical Society]] Distinguished Service Award, 2000<ref name="Haimo Citation"/>
* One of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]], 2002<ref name="Haimo Citation">
{{cite conference|title=Mathematical Association of America: Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|book-title=January 2002 Prizes and Awards|pages=36–40|publisher=Joint Mathematics Meetings|date=2002-01-07|location=San Diego, CA|url=https://www.ams.org/ams/2002-prizes.pdf|access-date=2008-09-16}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]; Ams.org, retrieved 2013-07-11.</ref>
